content:
If one supplier's plans materialize, some memory chips for Apple devices will be manufactured in the United States for the first time.

New reports indicate that Apple memory supplier SK Hynix is in talks with Intel, looking to use the chip plant Intel plans to build in Ohio...

According to a Reuters report, although details remain unclear at this stage, the Korean company produces both RAM and flash memory chips for Apple devices.

Some processors used in Apple devices are already manufactured in the United States, but due to restrictions on foreign companies accessing TSMC's most advanced processes, these processors can only be used in older models. However, DRAM or NAND flash memory chips are not affected by this restriction, as Apple uses industry-standard versions.

However, the report notes that the plans may face opposition from the South Korean government, as South Korea may share Taiwan's concerns about exporting chip manufacturing technology, even for older process nodes.

SK Hynix says nothing has been finalized. Intel declined to comment on the report, but confirmed it will continue to push forward with development plans for its Ohio project.
